statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-21218 (GHSA-qvhc-9v3j-5rfw) is a .NET security feature bypass in System.Security.Cryptography.Cose: a crafted payload can bypass the library's security checks. Microsoft fixed the .NET 9 package in 9.0.13 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-qvhc-9v3j-5rfw, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/380, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.13/9.0.13.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: System.Security.Cryptography.Cose.dll appears in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, inside the System.Security.Cryptography.Cose NuGet package (implementation and reference assembly), and in no other package; it is not part of the .NET or ASP.NET Core shared frameworks. In 9.0.12-r0 that package is 9.0.12, which is affected; from 9.0.13-r0 on, the version is 9.0.13 or later, with Microsoft's fix. The range ends at 9.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
